answer: Give every agent a paper watermark registry. A newcomer presses 20 sheets, each with one watermark no other sheet has, in juniper-resin ink that smudges if copied. Two papermakers hold each sheet to the light and log it only if both agree it is genuine. A forged watermark burns that sheet's credit and freezes rewards for 30 days. Twelve verified sheets unlock full rewards, and anyone can re-check a sheet's plume of fibers in the public registry. Faking 1,000 agents needs 20,000 sheets and 40,000 inspections. Trust grows like a glacier from snowfall, slow and impossible to fake overnight.
